policy.scope: serve standard stdio path with verified original SDK methods and a native standard stdout stream
policy.serialization: unchanged official SDK JSONRPCMessage.model_dump_json and newline
policy.encoding: same owned native UTF-8 TextIOWrapper over the standard stdout binary buffer
policy.write_and_flush: one default anyio.to_thread.run_sync operation calls the original native write(data), then flush(), in that order
policy.flush_frequency: every successful message is flushed immediately; no batching across responses
policy.followup_flush: skip only the immediately following SDK flush already completed successfully by that write; standalone flush and a flush after failed write/flush delegate normally
policy.thread_cancellation: preserve default non-abandoning worker behavior; propagate write and flush errors; do not change limiters or cancellation options
policy.lifecycle: official stdio_server(stdout=adapter), unchanged lowlevel server initialization/lifespan/context/handlers; no explicit closing of standard process handles
policy.fallback: unknown SDK version, replaced or custom SDK method, unsupported standard-stream identity or custom stdout uses the original FastMCP.run(transport=stdio) path
unchanged: C5 bounded exact-count memo and cold/warm policy

registered_memo_policy.ownership: one MemoryBook connection; both encoders share limits
registered_memo_policy.cold_warm_boundary: Preserve original connection lifecycles, configuration order and shuffled query orders. Each fresh connection starts empty; native later token configurations can reuse prior counts on that connection. Each actual MCP configuration starts a fresh official server process. No extra prewarming, no discarded first queries, and no selective cache clearing.
registered_memo_policy.diagnostics: Save native memo state before/after every configuration outside timing, including start/hits/misses/evictions/entries/text bytes and cold-prefix observations where available. Preserve original actual SDK MCP command, protocol and measured envelope; private memo counters are not exposed over MCP. Its cold process boundary and actual process RSS are recorded. Do not describe this experiment as disabling every cache.
registered_memo_policy.continuation: C6 retains the exact C5 token memo. No additional persistent feature or statement cache is introduced.

prior_c4.boundary: Original complete development summary verified. C4 formal runner was never bound or executed; no C4 formal acceptance is inferred and development arithmetic is not rerun here.

rejected_c3.boundary: Original committed summary and rejection verified; C3 retrieval and raw-ledger arithmetic are not rerun by this C7 audit.

sample_retention: All 16 workers, all 56,784 calls and 113,568 start/finish events were checked in original order. No sample, round, adverse value or failed gate was dropped; no measurement was repeated.
limitations: Independent arithmetic and digest/ledger/provenance audit of saved measurements; source text, tokenization and returned payload bodies are not rerun.
The hashes compare complete stored non-timing responses and recorded invariant fields; this is not a new retrieval-quality evaluation.
One host and old regression queries; no statistical-significance, new-domain or whole-product competitor-speed claim.

Native memo snapshots include each retained first query and natural reuse across later native configurations. No query is added or omitted. They do not establish MCP memo hit rates or a whole-process 2 MiB memory limit.
A resource-review flag remains a release decision requiring explicit evidence assessment, not an automatic waiver.
